items.title: The EULAR points to consider regarding the development of criteria for the assessment of the disease activity in adult-onset Still's disease.
items.abstract: This study aims to formulate European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (EULAR) points to consider (PtCs) regarding the development of criteria for the assessment of the disease activity in adult-onset Still's disease (AOSD). The Task Force consisted of 23 members from 7 different European countries. A systematic literature review and a 3-round Delphi exercise involving European Experts were conducted to support the formulation of overarching principles and PtCs. Based on retrieved evidence and Experts' opinions, results of Delphi Rounds, and discussions, 3 overarching principles and 11 PtCs were developed. The Task Force agreed on the importance of an appropriate definition for the disease activity in AOSD to be valid, reliable, and easily transferable in a clinical setting. The development of specific criteria for the assessment of disease activity should include a precise definition of the clinical features that could better describe the patient condition. A clear definition of disease activity would help clinicians to adjust therapy and to identify refractory patients. A validated assessment of the disease activity is important to establish specifically designed and powered studies for comprehensive management of patients with AOSD. A uniform and reproducible definition of remission may facilitate the inclusion of a new therapeutic target into daily practice and clinical trials. The EULAR PtCs were produced regarding the development of criteria for the assessment of the disease activity in AOSD, to provide the basis for a clinical tool to be readily, reliably, and easily applied in clinical settings in order to improve patient management.

items.title: Copper single-atom carbon dots hydrogel resets oxidative and immune homeostasis for rheumatoid arthritis therapy.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis pathogenesis is perpetuated by a self-sustaining oxidative stress-immunodysregulation circuit. To address the limitations of conventional antioxidants, including unclear catalytic structures and single catalytic activity, we engineered copper single-atom carbon dots via topological transformation of sodium copper chlorophyllin. Encapsulated within a pH-responsive injectable hydrogel, this system achieves targeted delivery to inflamed joints, where it simultaneously scavenges superoxide anions and hydrogen peroxide, breaking the reactive oxygen species-inflammation cycle. Treatment reprograms macrophage polarization, suppresses pathogenic B-cell infiltration, and mitigates cartilage erosion. By integrating nature-inspired atomic catalysis with intelligent biomaterial engineering, this approach establishes a paradigm for resetting oxidative-immune microenvironments in autoimmune diseases.

items.title: Allergic profile and pre-diagnostic exposure to allergen-specific immunotherapy in eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA): a single-centre retrospective observational study.
items.abstract: Eosinophilic Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis (EGPA) combines asthma, eosinophilic inflammation and small- to medium-vessel vasculitis. The relationship between conventional allergic phenotypes, allergen-specific immunotherapy (AIT) and subsequent EGPA remains uncertain. To describe specialist-adjudicated allergic manifestations in a selected EGPA cohort and explore whether pre-diagnostic AIT exposure was associated with age at EGPA onset or clinical phenotype. We retrospectively analysed 53 patients with expert-diagnosed EGPA, complete historical records and an allergy evaluation adequate to classify aeroallergen sensitisation, respiratory allergy, food allergy and drug hypersensitivity. Continuous variables were assessed for normality and compared using Mann-Whitney U tests; categorical variables were compared using Fisher exact tests. Analyses were exploratory. Twenty-five patients (47.2%) had at least one recorded allergic manifestation. Aeroallergen sensitisation was present in 14/53 (26.4%), food allergy in 4/53 (7.5%), drug hypersensitivity in 13/53 (24.5%) and another specialist-adjudicated allergic manifestation in 1/53 (1.9%); categories overlapped. Thirteen of 14 aeroallergen-sensitized patients had multiple sensitisations. Thirteen patients were considered eligible for AIT and 7 received AIT before EGPA diagnosis. The median interval from AIT initiation to EGPA diagnosis was 13.1 years (interquartile range 5.5-20.0). No AIT-related adverse reaction was documented in available records. Exploratory comparisons did not identify statistically significant differences between allergic and non-allergic patients or between AIT-treated and AIT-eligible untreated patients. In this selected single-centre cohort, allergic manifestations were frequent, but the inclusion process precludes population-level prevalence estimates. No association between pre-diagnostic AIT exposure and age at EGPA onset or exploratory phenotype measures was observed. No signals of potentially AIT-triggered cases were found. However, the very small AIT subgroup, retrospective design and non-systematic safety ascertainment do not exclude clinically relevant effects and do not establish causality or AIT safety. Key Points • Allergic manifestations, particularly aeroallergen sensitisation and drug hypersensitivity, were frequent in this selected single-centre EGPA cohort. • Allergic status was not associated with a clearly distinct EGPA phenotype, although subgroup comparisons were exploratory and limited by the small sample size. • No association was observed between previous allergen-specific immunotherapy and the age or clinical pattern of EGPA onset.

items.title: Unilateral adrenal haemorrhage during bridging anticoagulation in primary antiphospholipid syndrome: a case-based review.
items.abstract: Antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) is a major cause of acquired thrombophilia and is frequently associated with recurrent venous thromboembolism requiring long-term anticoagulation. We report a 42-year-old man with primary APS and recurrent pulmonary embolism and deep vein thrombosis who developed acute right upper-quadrant abdominal pain during peri-procedural bridging anticoagulation with enoxaparin. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated acute-to-subacute unilateral right adrenal haemorrhage without evidence of abdominal trauma, malignancy or infection. The patient remained haemodynamically stable and did not develop adrenal insufficiency. This case highlights the complexity of anticoagulation management in high-risk APS patients and emphasises the importance of considering adrenal haemorrhage in APS patients presenting with abdominal pain during anticoagulation modification. A review of previously reported unilateral APS-associated adrenal haemorrhage cases is also presented. Key Points • Unilateral adrenal haemorrhage is a rare manifestation of primary antiphospholipid syndrome. • Bridging anticoagulation may represent a vulnerable period for adrenal haemorrhage in high-risk APS. • Early CT/MRI imaging and assessment of adrenal function are essential. • Conservative management with careful reintroduction of anticoagulation may lead to favourable outcomes.

items.title: Double-negative B cells mediate the causal association between rheumatoid arthritis and interstitial lung disease: a two-step Mendelian randomization mediation study.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) elevates interstitial lung disease (ILD) risk, yet the underlying mediating immune cells remain unknown. This study sought peripheral immune phenotypes driving the causal pathway from RA to ILD. A two-step Mendelian randomization (MR) mediation analysis was performed using European GWAS data: RA (14,361 cases/43,923), 731 immune cell traits, and ILD from FinnGen R13 (6,733 cases/493,453). Step 1 applied inverse variance weighted (IVW) MR to estimate RA effects on immune cells; Step 2 tested immune cell effects on ILD. Mediation was validated via joint significance and parametric bootstrapping (10,000 resamples) with BCa 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RA exerted a causal risk-increasing effect on ILD (β = 0.166, P = 4.26 × 10⁻⁸). Fifty-three immune traits showed nominal significance in Step 1, 15 passing FDR correction. CD19⁺IgD⁻CD27⁻ DN B cells reached nominal significance (P = 0.028) but not FDR significance (q = 0.512) in Step 1, yet were the only trait significantly associated with ILD in Step 2 (β₂ = 0.060, P = 0.027). Bootstrapping verified a small but significant indirect effect (β = 0.0039, 95% BCa CI 0.0009-0.0153, P = 0.050; mediation proportion = 2.3%), consistent across sensitivity tests. DN B cells partially mediate the causal RA-ILD relationship. Our genetic evidence highlights B cell dysfunction as a mechanistic link and identifies DN B cells as candidate biomarkers for RA-related interstitial lung complications. Key Points • Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is associated with elevated interstitial lung disease (ILD) risk, yet the underlying causal pathway remains poorly defined. • A two-step Mendelian randomization mediation design was applied to identify double-negative (DN) B cells (CD19⁺IgD⁻CD27⁻) as a potential mediator linking RA to ILD. • Genetically predisposed RA was causally associated with increased DN B cell proportions, which in turn were associated with higher ILD risk. • These findings indicate DN B cells may serve as a potential immunological link between RA and ILD, meriting further investigation as a candidate direction for early intervention research.

items.title: Deguelin Alleviates Renal Tubular Epithelial Cell Injury in Lupus Nephritis by Inhibiting the PI3K/Akt Signaling Pathway.
items.abstract: Lupus nephritis (LN) is one of the most serious complications of systemic lupus erythematosus. Circadian rhythm disorders are related to the pathogenesis of LN. This study aims to identify the core circadian rhythm-related genes in LN and identify the potential natural active compounds for LN treatment. In the present study, cyclin A2 (CCNA2) and cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor 3 (CDKN3) were identified as the core targets most related to the circadian rhythm of LN. Both of them were upregulated in blood and kidney tissue samples in LN and had high diagnostic efficacy. Deguelin had strong binding capabilities with CCNA2 and CDKN3 proteins. Deguelin could dose-dependently alleviate lipopolysaccharide-induced human kidney-2 (HK-2) cell damage, inhibit cell apoptosis and the release of inflammatory factors, downregulate the mRNA and protein expression levels of core genes CCNA2 and CDKN3, and inhibit the activation of the phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)/Akt signaling pathway. The protective effect of deguelin could be reversed by AKT activator SC79 treatment. In summary, CCNA2 and CDKN3 are core genes related to the circadian rhythm in LN. Deguelin probably alleviates renal tubular epithelial cell injury by modulating the expression levels of core genes CCNA2 and CDKN3, inhibiting the activation of the PI3K/Akt signaling pathway, and thus has the potential to become a therapeutic agent for LN.

items.title: Assessing the quality of end-of-life care in systemic sclerosis.
items.abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a rare autoimmune disease with the highest mortality among rheumatic diseases, yet little is known about the quality of end-of-life care in SSc. To evaluate end-of-life care in SSc against the Australian National Consensus Statement's Essential Elements for high-quality end-of-life care and compare care between palliative care unit (PCU) and non-PCU deaths. This retrospective single-centre study included adults with SSc who died between 2013 and 2023 at a tertiary SSc referral centre. Terminal admission records for expected deaths were mapped to the National Consensus domains. Fisher exact and Mann-Whitney U tests compared PCU and non-PCU deaths. Thirty-three patients died. Six unexpected deaths were excluded, leaving 15 PCU and 12 non-PCU deaths. Multidisciplinary involvement was extensive, particularly from rheumatology and allied health. Palliative care engagement was common, goals of care were frequently reviewed and communication about dying with next-of-kin occurred in most cases. Patients dying outside the PCU had lower rates of documented recognition of dying, significantly greater intensive care involvement and more frequent medical emergency team calls. They also received more potentially non-beneficial investigations and treatments during the final 48 h of life and incurred substantially higher terminal admission costs. End-of-life care in SSc was broadly consistent with the National Consensus standards, identifying strong rheumatology involvement, multidisciplinary care and frequent palliative care referral. However, differences in care according to site of death highlight opportunities to increase proactive palliative care involvement and regular review of goals of care to ensure high-quality end-of-life care across all settings.

items.title: Patient perspectives on simultaneous methotrexate-folic acid intake to improve adherence in rheumatoid arthritis: a cross-sectional survey.
items.abstract: To assess real-world adherence to folic acid (FA) supplementation with methotrexate (MTX) and patient perceptions of a simplified, same-day dosing strategy in RA. We conducted a cross-sectional online survey co-designed with patient representatives and distributed by the French patient association AFPric. RA patients treated with MTX were eligible. The questionnaire captured MTX and FA regimens, omissions, adverse events and attitudes toward same-day MTX and FA administration. Analyses were descriptive with prespecified subgroup comparisons. Among 967 respondents (86.8% women; mean age 62.4 years), 86.7% reported once-weekly FA supplementation. Overall, 25.5% reported at least occasional FA omission, with omissions more frequent among long-term MTX users. Nausea after MTX was reported by 46.6% of respondents and by 52.6% of those reporting FA omissions. A same-day MTX and FA regimen was perceived as simpler by 30.5% and 41.5% believed it could reduce FA omission. Overall, 64.8% indicated that they would be willing to participate in a randomised controlled trial evaluating simultaneous administration. One in four people with RA treated with MTX reported FA omissions. Many respondents believed that a same-day regimen could reduce FA omissions, and interest in participating in a clinical trial was high. These findings support the feasibility of prospectively evaluating whether same-day MTX and FA administration may improve adherence and tolerability in selected patients, particularly those receiving once-weekly FA supplementation, without compromising MTX effectiveness.

items.title: Identification of the Proapoptotic Mechanism of Astragalosides in Rheumatoid Arthritis Therapy Based on HPLC, Bioinformatics and Network Pharmacology.
items.abstract: Astragalosides (ASTs), principal active saponins derived from Astragalus, exert prominent therapeutic efficacy against Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA). However, few studies have investigated the molecular mechanism of ASTs in RA therapy. AST components were qualitatively and quantitatively analyzed by HPLC. RA-related Differentially Expressed Genes (DEGs) were acquired from the GSE77298 dataset, and AST target genes were predicted via multiple databases. Core hub genes and signaling pathways were screened through bioinformatics analyses, including GO/KEGG enrichment, PPI network and MCODE modularity analysis. Molecular docking was performed to evaluate the binding affinity between ASTs and core apoptotic genes. Cell phenotypic assays, qRT-PCR, Western blot and CASP8 siRNA interference experiments were conducted to validate the regulatory effect of ASTs on the CASP8-ATM-XIAP-CASP3 axis in MH7A cells. In total, 5781 DEGs were obtained from the GSE77298 dataset, 496 ASTs-related genes were predicted, among which 156 intersected. They were enriched in 3345 significant GO terms and 121 significant KEGG pathways. Bioinformatic and experimental analyses validated that ATM, CASP8, and XIAP mediate AST-induced MH7A cell apoptosis via the CASP8-ATM-XIAP-CASP3 axis. ASTs decrease cellular proliferation and induce apoptosis in MH7A cells. Moreover, ASTs reduced the expression of XIAP and increased the expression of ATM and CASP8 at both the mRNA and protein levels. In addition, ASTs reversed the effects of siRNA-mediated CASP8 silencing on the mRNA expression of CASP3, ATM, and XIAP. ASTs can promote apoptosis in MH7A cells, and the underlying mechanism may involve regulation of the CASP8-ATM-XIAP-CASP3 signaling axis.

items.title: Echocardiographic characteristics and clinical features of cardiac involvement in Behçet's disease: a retrospective single-center case series.
items.abstract: Cardiac involvement in Behçet's disease (BD) is uncommon but potentially life-threatening and may mimic other cardiovascular disorders, complicating early diagnosis. This study aimed to characterize the clinical and echocardiographic features, treatment, pathological findings, and clinical outcomes of patients with cardiac BD, with particular emphasis on the utility of echocardiography in raising diagnostic suspicion. We retrospectively screened 186 patients with diagnosed or suspected BD at The Second Affiliated Hospital of Jiangxi Medical College, Nanchang University between October 2020 and January 2026. Of the 112 patients who underwent transthoracic echocardiography, 23 met the International Criteria for BD and were determined by multidisciplinary evaluation to have cardiac lesions attributable to BD after exclusion of alternative etiologies. Clinical, laboratory, electrocardiographic, echocardiographic, pathological, treatment, and follow-up data were descriptively analyzed. The cohort was predominantly male (82.6%), with a mean age of 43.5±13.1 years. The most frequent systemic manifestations were oral ulcers (95.7%), cutaneous lesions (73.9%), and genital ulcers (60.9%). Elevated inflammatory markers, including erythrocyte sedimentation rate (87.0%) and C-reactive protein (82.6%), were frequently observed. B-type natriuretic peptide levels were elevated in 91.3% of patients. Among the 19 patients without a history of cardiac surgery, severe aortic regurgitation was the predominant echocardiographic finding (94.7%) and was most often associated with aortic valve prolapse (78.9%). Other echocardiographic findings included aortic cusp aneurysm with perforation (15.8%), echo-free spaces around the aortic root (21.1%), aortic root and/or ascending aortic dilatation (63.2%), pulmonary artery dilatation (52.6%), left-sided chamber enlargement (84.2%), four-chamber enlargement (10.5%), and reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (21.1%). Among the four patients with a history of cardiac or great-vessel surgery, all three who had undergone aortic valve replacement developed prosthetic valve dehiscence with severe paravalvular leakage within 2-6 months of surgery. Pathological examination of 14 surgical specimens revealed inflammatory-destructive changes involving the aortic wall and valve, characterized by fibrosis, hyalinization, myxoid degeneration, and chronic inflammatory cell infiltration. All patients received glucocorticoid-based immunosuppressive therapy, and 17 also underwent surgical treatment. At the last follow-up, 16 of 23 patients were alive and clinically stable, four were lost to follow-up, and three had died. In this case series, cardiac BD was mainly characterized by destructive valvulo-aortic lesions, particularly severe aortic regurgitation associated with cusp prolapse and periannular or aortic root abnormalities. Echocardiography plays an important role in defining lesion morphology and severity, detecting postoperative prosthetic valve complications, and identifying structural abnormalities that may raise suspicion for cardiac BD in the appropriate clinical context.

items.title: When the Heart Reveals Lupus: Severe Dilated Cardiomyopathy as the Initial Manifestation of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
items.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a multisystem autoimmune disease with heterogeneous cardiovascular involvement, while clinically overt lupus myocarditis remains uncommon. We report the case of a 50-year-old woman with no previous cardiovascular or autoimmune disease who presented with acute decompensated heart failure after a two-year history of progressive exertional dyspnea. Transthoracic echocardiography revealed severe biventricular dilated cardiomyopathy with a left ventricular ejection fraction of 21% and profoundly reduced global longitudinal strain (-5.0%). Cardiac biomarkers were markedly elevated, whereas coronary angiography showed normal epicardial coronary arteries. Autoimmune testing revealed high-titer antinuclear antibodies, elevated anti-double-stranded DNA and anti-Smith antibodies, and complement consumption, despite the absence of typical cutaneous, articular, renal, or neurological manifestations of SLE. Cardiac magnetic resonance demonstrated subepicardial late gadolinium enhancement involving the anterolateral wall in a non-ischemic distribution. The integration of clinical, immunological, coronary, and multimodality imaging findings supported clinically suspected lupus myocarditis as the inaugural manifestation of previously unrecognized SLE. Guideline-directed heart failure therapy and immunosuppressive treatment were initiated, with early clinical improvement and a decrease in cardiac biomarkers. In the absence of endomyocardial biopsy, the diagnosis remained clinically and imaging-supported rather than histologically confirmed. This case highlights an unusual presentation of SLE revealed by severe biventricular dilated cardiomyopathy and emphasizes the pivotal role of multimodality imaging and targeted autoimmune testing in identifying an inflammatory etiology of otherwise unexplained non-ischemic cardiomyopathy.

items.title: Isolated Medial Ankle Tenosynovitis of the Flexor Digitorum and Posterior Tibialis Tendons: A Case Report of the Role of Early Musculoskeletal Ultrasound in Identifying Anti-citrullinated Protein Antibody (ACPA)-Positive At-Risk Rheumatoid Arthritis.
items.abstract: Tenosynovitis is a recognized feature of rheumatoid arthritis (RA), yet it typically presents alongside symmetric polyarticular synovitis. Isolated focal tenosynovitis as the primary and initial manifestation of RA is uncommon and frequently leads to diagnostic delays. We present the case of a 62-year-old female who presented with localized right ankle pain in the absence of systemic joint involvement or elevated inflammatory markers. While the rheumatoid factor was negative and both the erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein levels were within normal limits, musculoskeletal ultrasound revealed focal tenosynovitis of the flexor digitorum and posterior tibialis tendons, accompanied by possible early erosive changes of the medial malleolus. Markedly elevated titers of anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide (112 U) and mutated citrullinated vimentin (171 U) antibodies supported the diagnosis. The patient responded rapidly to prednisone and was subsequently transitioned to methotrexate. This case emphasizes that isolated tenosynovitis can be the early presenting feature of seropositive RA. It underscores the critical role of advanced serologic testing and high-resolution imaging in identifying early-stage disease when traditional clinical markers are absent, allowing for timely intervention to prevent irreversible structural damage.

items.title: Reverse Total Shoulder Arthroplasty in a 25-Year-Old Woman With Seropositive Rheumatoid Arthritis After Prior Age-Based Surgical Deferral.
items.abstract: Reverse total shoulder arthroplasty (RTSA) in very young adults with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is uncommon because of concerns regarding implant longevity and lifetime revision burden, and outcomes data in patients younger than 30 years remain limited. We report the case of a 25-year-old woman with seropositive RA who developed rapid, destructive monoarticular involvement of the right shoulder despite treatment with disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs) and biologic therapy. Imaging demonstrated complete glenohumeral joint space obliteration, humeral head collapse, erosive changes, and rotator cuff insufficiency. An initial shoulder surgeon declined arthroplasty based on her age and anticipated revision risk. Following staged diagnostic arthroscopy, definitive RTSA was performed in December 2023 without complication. At four months, near-full active forward elevation was restored. At two-year follow-up, the American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons (ASES) score was 80/100 (pain 3/10; activities of daily living 27/30), and the Single Assessment Numeric Evaluation (SANE) score was 95%. No instability, infection, or mechanical failure occurred. This case demonstrates that RTSA can provide excellent early and mid-term functional outcomes in carefully selected very young patients with end-stage inflammatory shoulder disease and may help inform surgical decision-making when age is the primary barrier to intervention.

items.title: Inflammatory and total immunoglobulin biomarker domains in systemic sclerosis vasculopathy: a phenotype-based cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: To characterize inflammatory and total immunoglobulin-domain profiles across clinically defined vasculopathy phenotypes in SSc using a phenotype-oriented framework. In this retrospective cross-sectional study, 314 patients with SSc fulfilling the 2013 ACR/EULAR criteria were classified into four vasculopathy phenotypes: no DU/gangrene/clinically diagnosed PAH/SRC-defined overt vasculopathy ("none"), peripheral only, visceral only, and mixed. Inflammatory and total immunoglobulin-domain scores were prespecified as the mean of standardised ESR and hs-CRP, and IgG and IgA, respectively. Associations between domain scores and phenotypes were evaluated using adjusted multinomial logistic regression, with prespecified binary and sensitivity analyses used as supportive analyses. Omnibus comparisons across the four phenotypes, ESR, hs-CRP, CAR, and IgG remained significant after FDR correction, whereas albumin, IgA, and ACA showed nominal differences only. Descriptively, ESR and hs-CRP were higher in visceral-involvement phenotypes, IgG was highest in the visceral-only group, and IgA was highest in the mixed group. In adjusted multinomial models, each 1-SD increase in the inflammatory domain score was associated with visceral-only phenotype versus none (OR 1.49, 95% CI 1.06-2.10, p = 0.021) and mixed phenotype versus none (OR 1.60, 95% CI 1.03-2.47, p = 0.035) in the single-domain model, while each 1-SD increase in the total immunoglobulin-domain score was associated with visceral-only phenotype versus none (OR 1.43, 95% CI 1.02-2.02, p = 0.039). These multinomial associations did not remain robust after FDR correction and were attenuated in the joint-domain model. In the prespecified supportive binary analyses, the clearest associations were observed for visceral involvement versus none: inflammatory domain OR 1.59 (95% CI 1.19-2.14) and total immunoglobulin-domain OR 1.53 (95% CI 1.14-2.06). Sensitivity analyses showed no material direction reversal but indicated attenuation after extended adjustment. Circulating inflammatory and total immunoglobulin-domain scores showed a directionally consistent association with clinically defined, predominantly clinically diagnosed PAH-weighted visceral vascular involvement in this inpatient SSc cohort. These exploratory cross-sectional findings require confirmation in prospectively phenotyped cohorts. Key Points • We classified systemic sclerosis vasculopathy into clinically defined phenotypes based on structural peripheral ischaemic damage and clinically diagnosed PAH/SRC-defined visceral vascular involvement. • Circulating inflammatory and total immunoglobulin-domain enrichment was more evident in clinically defined, predominantly PAH-weighted visceral-involvement phenotypes than in peripheral-only disease. • Peripheral-only phenotype, defined narrowly by structural ischaemic damage endpoints, showed limited domain-level enrichment after adjustment. • Attenuation in joint-domain models suggests partial overlap between systemic inflammatory burden and total immunoglobulin-related signals.

items.title: Clinical characteristics and associated factors of difficult-to-treat rheumatoid arthritis: a cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: This study aimed to describe the clinical characteristics and explore factors cross-sectionally associated with difficult-to-treat rheumatoid arthritis (D2T RA) in a Chinese population, providing evidence for characterizing the clinical phenotype and identifying current associated factors in a Chinese population. A cross-sectional study was conducted, enrolling RA patients treated at the Rheumatology Department of Dongfang Hospital, Beijing University of Chinese Medicine, from September 2022 to September 2024. Based on the 2020 EULAR criteria, adapted in accordance with the 2021 Chinese consensus on refractory rheumatoid arthritis, patients were categorized into a D2T RA group (n = 61) and a conventional RA group (n = 182). An exploratory subsample (n = 6 per group) underwent plasma cytokine analysis via Luminex assay. Data on demographics, disease activity measures, laboratory inflammatory parameters, comorbidities, and medication use were collected. Plasma cytokine levels were measured using Luminex technology. Statistical analysis was performed using R software, and associated factors were analyzed via univariate and multivariate logistic regression. Patients in the D2T RA group were significantly younger than those in the RA group (P = 0.009) and exhibited significantly higher values in swollen joint count, VAS pain score, DAS28-ESR, CDAI, and SDAI (all P < 0.05). The prevalence of osteoporosis was significantly higher in the D2T RA group (85.25% vs. 61.54%, P = 0.001), and the usage of JAK inhibitors was also notably elevated (85.25% vs. 1.10%, P = 0.027). Regarding inflammatory markers, except for elevated plateletcrit, no significant differences were observed in CRP, ESR, IL-6, or composite inflammation indices between groups. Exploratory cytokine analysis (n = 6 per group) showed that IL-6 and IL-17A levels were significantly elevated in the D2T RA group compared to healthy volunteers, whereas no significant differences were observed between the RA and D2T RA groups. Multivariate logistic regression identified that older age was associated with lower odds of D2T RA (OR = 0.94, 95% CI: 0.91-0.98, P =  0.011), while OP remained independently associated with higher odds (OR = 4.95, 95% CI: 1.96-12.15, P < 0.001). In this single-center Chinese cohort, D2T RA was characterized by younger age, higher disease activity, and a higher comorbidity rate of osteoporosis. Younger age and comorbid osteoporosis were cross-sectionally associated with D2T RA. These findings may assist clinicians in recognizing high-risk clinical phenotypes and inform the development of targeted intervention strategies, but require confirmation in prospective, multicenter studies.

items.title: Bimekizumab efficacy across GRAPPA domains to 3 years in patients with psoriatic arthritis: a post hoc analysis of two phase 3 studies.
items.abstract: To evaluate the long-term efficacy of bimekizumab in patients with psoriatic arthritis (PsA) across the Group for Research and Assessment of Psoriasis and Psoriatic Arthritis (GRAPPA) domains, PsA-related conditions, and comorbidities. Post hoc analysis of pooled data from BE OPTIMAL (NCT03895203; biologic-naïve patients) and BE COMPLETE (NCT03896581; patients with prior inadequate response/intolerance to tumour necrosis factor inhibitors) phase 3 studies, and their open-label extension BE VITAL (NCT04009499), which assessed subcutaneous bimekizumab 160 mg every 4 weeks in patients with active PsA. Efficacy was assessed to 3 years (Week 148) across GRAPPA core domains, PsA-related conditions (inflammatory bowel disease [IBD] and uveitis), and inflammatory markers of cardiovascular risk. Among 1,112 bimekizumab-treated patients with PsA, improvements were sustained across the GRAPPA core domains to 3 years. Resolution of swollen and tender joint count at 3 years was achieved by 59.2% and 34.6% of patients, respectively, while 54.8% achieved ≥50% improvement from baseline in American College of Rheumatology response criteria (modified non-responder imputation [mNRI]). Enthesitis (LEI=0) and dactylitis (LDI=0) resolution was also achieved by 56.6% (mNRI) and 68.6% (NRI) of patients, respectively. A high proportion of patients achieved skin and nail psoriasis clearance (PASI100: 64.6%; mNAPSI=0: 68.0%; mNRI). IBD and uveitis events were rare, and inflammatory cardiovascular risk marker improvements were sustained. Bimekizumab provided long-term, sustained disease control across GRAPPA domains and systemic inflammation markers in patients with PsA, with low rates of IBD and uveitis, supporting its use as a long-term treatment for the heterogeneous manifestations of PsA. items.title: Immunosuppressant-refractory Multifaceted Immune Dysregulations for Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
items.abstract: While the systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), a severe autoimmune disease, is known to relapse frequently after treatment, none of the previous single-cell studies have examined the immune dynamics and their potential contribution to this relapse in the real clinical setting. To address this issue, here we employed single-cell multi-omics profiling to delineate immune repertoire dynamics during the immunosuppressant-based standard of care. Further analysis showed that the canonical therapy fails to restore various critical abnormalities, including the drop in mutational load of B and plasma cells, and the clonal expansion of CD4+ Th1 and CD8+ memory T cells. We also integrated our data with published SLE datasets to compile a comprehensive SLE immune atlas of about 1.6 million cells. Our study provides valuable data and sheds light on the underlying multifaceted unresolved dysregulation upon SLE immunosuppressant therapy under the real clinical setting; such dysregulation may further contribute to the high post-treatment relapse rate and thus call for additional target-specific treatment strategies.

items.title: Retro-Odontoid Calcium Pyrophosphate Deposition Pseudotumor Presenting with Isolated Hypoglossal Nerve Palsy: A Case Report.
items.abstract: Introduction Retro-odontoid pseudotumor is a rare non-neoplastic lesion of the craniocervical junction, most commonly associated with inflammatory or degenerative conditions. Calcium pyrophosphate deposition (CPPD) disease is an underrecognized cause. Cranial nerve involvement is uncommon, and isolated hypoglossal nerve palsy is exceedingly rare. Case Report We report a 75-year-old woman who presented with a 5-month history of occipital headache followed by acute onset of left hypoglossal nerve palsy. Imaging revealed a partially calcified retro-odontoid mass extending toward the left hypoglossal canal. Laboratory and rheumatologic investigations were unremarkable. The patient underwent posterior C1-C2 fusion with biopsy. Histopathology confirmed CPPD disease. At 6-month follow-up, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) demonstrated significant regression of the lesion accompanied by clinical improvement. Conclusion This case highlights that posterior stabilization alone may provide effective indirect decompression and promote lesion regression while avoiding more invasive anterior approaches.

items.title: Haemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis Triggered by Visceral Leishmaniasis Masquerading as Epstein-Barr Virus (EBV)-Associated Haemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis in Rheumatoid Arthritis: A Case Report and Literature Review.
items.abstract: Haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) is a life-threatening hyperinflammatory syndrome caused by uncontrolled immune activation. In adults, it is usually secondary to an underlying condition, such as infection, malignancy, or autoimmune disease. Identifying this trigger is essential, as treatment depends on the cause. Visceral leishmaniasis (VL) is a systemic parasitic infection that may mimic or trigger HLH, particularly in immunosuppressed patients. We report a 59-year-old man with seropositive rheumatoid arthritis, for which he received immunosuppressive treatment with methotrexate and etanercept. For eosinophilic asthma, he was treated with benralizumab. Four months after travelling to the Valencia region in Spain, the patient presented with high fever, marked splenomegaly and pancytopenia. Further laboratory findings showed progressive hyperferritinaemia, hypofibrinogenaemia, and hypertriglyceridaemia, together with haemophagocytosis on bone marrow examination, which supported the diagnosis of secondary HLH. Because Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) DNA was detected in peripheral blood, EBV-associated HLH was initially suspected, and treatment was started with rituximab, targeting potentially EBV-infected B cells, and dexamethasone to suppress the hyperinflammatory response. Further infectious work-up, however, revealed a strongly positive Leishmania serology. Leishmania polymerase chain reaction on the original bone marrow sample subsequently confirmed VL, despite the absence of amastigotes on Giemsa-stained microscopy. Treatment was redirected to liposomal amphotericin B; further HLH-directed immunosuppressive therapy was withheld, and corticosteroids were tapered. The patient became afebrile and showed progressive recovery of cytopenias and inflammatory markers. Detectable EBV DNA should not preclude investigation for alternative infectious triggers of HLH. In immunosuppressed patients with compatible epidemiological exposure, VL should remain in the differential diagnosis even when bone marrow microscopy is negative, as serology and molecular testing may be required for diagnosis.

items.title: A pediatric case of orbital inflammation and sinusitis- the diagnostic boundary between localized ANCA-associated vasculitis and IgG4-related disease.
items.abstract: ANCA-associated vasculitis (AAV) are characterized by necrotizing inflammation of small- and medium-sized blood vessels, frequently associated with antibodies against myeloperoxidase (MPO) or proteinase 3. In contrast, IgG4-related disease (IgG4-RD) is an immune-mediated fibroinflammatory condition that can affect virtually any organ and is histologically characterized by lymphoplasmacytic infiltrates enriched in IgG4-positive plasma cells. Both conditions may present with localized or systemic disease and share clinical and histopathological features, particularly in the head and neck region, making differential diagnosis challenging. We report the case of an 11-year-old girl who initially presented with bilateral orbital inflammation. Orbital biopsy demonstrated lymphoplasmacytic infiltrates, an elevated IgG4+/IgG+ plasma cell ratio, and obliterative phlebitis, suggestive of IgG4-RD. However, markedly elevated MPO-ANCA levels raised suspicion for AAV. Although glucocorticoid therapy initially achieved clinical improvement, relapses occurred, prompting treatment with rituximab. Subsequently, the patient developed rhinosinusitis, and nasal biopsy revealed lymphoplasmacytic inflammation with multinucleated giant cells, consistent with granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA). Treatment was intensified with mycophenolate mofetil and corticosteroids, resulting in remission. This case highlights the diagnostic and therapeutic challenges posed by overlapping features of AAV and IgG4-RD.

items.title: When SLE patients have rosacea - key distinguishing features.
items.abstract: Facial erythema associated with antinuclear antibody (ANA) positivity frequently prompts referral to Rheumatology due to suspicion of acute cutaneous lupus erythematosus (ACLE). However, patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) may present with malar rash that clinically overlaps with rosacea. Because these conditions differ substantially in pathophysiology, prognosis, treatment, and follow-up requirements, distinguishing between them is essential for accurate diagnosis and management. This review summarizes the key clinical, dermoscopic, and histopathological features that aid in differentiating rosacea from ACLE. Correct differentiation between rosacea and ACLE is critical because rosacea is primarily managed with trigger avoidance, topical therapies, and oral antibiotics, whereas ACLE often requires immunosuppressive therapy and long-term systemic monitoring. Misdiagnosis may therefore result in either unnecessary immunosuppression or delayed treatment of systemic autoimmune disease.

items.title: Manifestations and predictors of vascular involvement in Behçet's disease.
items.abstract: Behçet´s disease (BD) is a variable vessel vasculitis in which vascular involvement (VBD) occurs in up to 40% of patients and represents a poor prognosis marker. Predictors of VBD have been poorly defined. We aimed to characterise VBD patients and to identify predictors of this clinical subtype. We performed a single-centre, retrospective study including patients fulfilling the 2013 International Criteria for BD, registered in the Rheumatic Diseases Portuguese Registry (Reuma.pt) between October 2014 and May 2023. VBD was defined as arterial or venous manifestations attributable to BD and confirmed by imaging. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify predictors of VBD. A total of 157 BD patients were included, 24 (15%) of whom had vascular involvement. Seven (5%) presented VBD as the inaugural manifestation. The median age at VBD onset was 36.0 years, occurring a median of 8.9 years after BD onset. Venous involvement (20/24, 83%) predominated over arterial (10/24, 42%). Deep vein thrombosis (50%) and superficial thrombophlebitis (42%) were the most common venous events. Arterial manifestations included aneurysms (21%), pulmonary thrombosis (13%) and pseudoaneurysms (8%). Multiple-vessel involvement (54%) and recurrent events (58%) were common. On comparison with patients without VBD, male sex (OR 3.99, 95%CI 1.55-10.28) and ocular involvement at disease onset (OR 3.90, 95%CI 1.29-11.72) emerged as predictors of VBD. In our BD cohort, vascular involvement occurred in 15% of patients, predominantly venous. Male sex and ocular involvement at disease onset were identified as predictors of VBD, suggesting their potential role as clinical markers for identifying high-risk patients.

items.title: Anifrolumab for refractory autoimmune hemolytic anemia in SPENCD-associated lupus: a case-based review.
items.abstract: Spondyloenchondrodysplasia (SPENCD) is a rare monogenic interferonopathy caused by biallelic ACP5 mutations, characterized by skeletal dysplasia, neurological involvement and immune dysregulation frequently manifesting as lupus-like disease. Autoimmune cytopenias, particularly autoimmune hemolytic anemia (AIHA), are among the most severe and treatment-refractory manifestations. Anifrolumab, a monoclonal antibody targeting interferon alpha receptor subunit 1 (IFNAR1), blocks signaling by all type I interferons and is approved for moderate-to-severe systemic lupus erythematosus. We report a 50-year-old man with SPENCD-associated lupus and refractory, transfusion-dependent AIHA who achieved sustained hematologic remission following anifrolumab initiation. Using this case as a framework, we discuss the pathophysiological basis of SPENCD, the spectrum and treatment challenges of its associated autoimmune cytopenias, and the evolving role of targeted therapies in monogenic interferonopathies, with particular emphasis on SPENCD, and summarize the published experience with anifrolumab in these disorders. Collectively, this case and the available literature provide preliminary support for IFNAR1 blockade as a mechanism-based, steroid-sparing strategy for refractory autoimmune cytopenias in SPENCD.

items.title: X-linked hypophosphataemia diagnosed in adulthood with coexisting seronegative rheumatoid arthritis: a diagnostic pitfall.
items.abstract: X-linked hypophosphataemia (XLH) is the most common inherited cause of renal phosphate wasting, typically diagnosed in childhood but occasionally identified in adulthood. We report a case of a 45-year-old woman with long-standing lower limb deformities, short stature, and diffuse joint pain. Laboratory evaluation revealed hypophosphataemia due to isolated renal phosphate wasting. Fibroblast growth factor 23 levels were markedly elevated. Imaging showed skeletal deformities and enthesopathic changes consistent with chronic XLH. Genetic testing identified a pathogenic PHEX variant (c.1645+1G>A), confirming the diagnosis. Treatment with oral phosphate and calcitriol resulted in biochemical improvement. During follow-up, the patient developed symmetrical erosive polyarthritis of the hands and wrists, consistent with seronegative rheumatoid arthritis superimposed on the underlying metabolic disorder. This case highlights the diagnostic challenge of XLH in adults, where musculoskeletal manifestations can closely mimic inflammatory arthritis. Recognising XLH as the underlying cause of chronic osteomalacia is essential to avoid inappropriate treatment and ensure timely management of coexisting conditions. New-onset erosive arthritis should prompt consideration of a concurrent inflammatory condition rather than attribution to the underlying metabolic disorder.

items.title: PD-1 inhibitor-associated Sicca syndrome mimicking Sjögren's disease successfully managed without immunotherapy withdrawal.
items.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) are increasingly associated with a broad spectrum of immune-related adverse events (irAEs), including rheumatic manifestations. We report a case of ICI-associated sicca syndrome (ICI-S) mimicking Sjögren's disease, with a brief literature review. The patient was a 70-year-old man with BRAF-mutated metastatic melanoma who developed inflammatory arthralgias followed by parotid and submandibular enlargement, severe xerostomia, and xerophthalmia, during pembrolizumab therapy. Treatment was withheld and low-dose glucocorticoids (GC) initiated, with rapid improvement of joint symptoms and gland swelling, although marked xerostomia persisted. The diagnostic work-up revealed elevated inflammatory markers and positive antinuclear antibodies (ANA), with negative anti-SSA/SSB. Salivary gland ultrasound showed grade 3 changes (OMERACT) and PET-CT confirmed bilateral sialadenitis. Minor salivary gland biopsy demonstrated T-cell-predominant lymphocytic infiltrate without CD20+ B cells, supporting an ICI-S rather than primary Sjögren's disease. Pembrolizumab rechallenge triggered a flare of sialadenitis and arthritis, controlled with GC reintroduction plus hydroxychloroquine and supportive measures. This case provides educational insights into the diagnostic differentiation between ICI-S and primary Sjögren's disease, supporting early recognition and appropriate management without compromising oncologic treatment.

items.title: Trends, outcomes, and disparities in hospitalizations among patients with Sjögren's syndrome: a national inpatient sample analysis (2016-2020).
items.abstract: Sjögren's syndrome (SS) is a systemic autoimmune disease with poorly characterized hospitalization outcomes in the United States. We aimed to characterize hospitalization trends, comorbidity profiles, organ-specific manifestations, predictors of in-hospital mortality, and racial, socioeconomic, and hospital-level disparities among SS-associated hospitalizations using the NIS 2016-2020 dataset. Retrospective cross-sectional analysis of the NIS (2016-2020). Adults with SS (ICD-10-CM M35.00-M35.0C) were identified across 40 diagnosis fields and matched 3:1 with non-autoimmune controls by age, sex, and year. Survey-weighted analyses included bivariate comparisons, Elixhauser comorbidity profiling, organ-specific phenotyping, nested multivariable logistic regression for mortality predictors, and adjusted disparities analyses using predictive margins. Among 272,630 weighted SS-associated hospitalizations (91.4% female, mean age 64.2 years), extraglandular manifestations were documented in 33.8%. Despite a significantly higher baseline comorbidity burden compared with 817,890 matched control hospitalizations, SS-associated admissions exhibited paradoxically lower crude in-hospital mortality (2.13% vs. 2.59%, p<0.001). However, within the SS cohort, acute complications were associated with substantial mortality risk in the fully adjusted model: independent predictors included mechanical ventilation (OR 21.08), sepsis (OR 2.80), stroke (OR 2.78), malignancy (OR 2.46), and interstitial lung disease (OR 2.10). Significant disparities persisted after multivariable adjustment: Asian/Pacific Islander hospitalizations had higher mortality odds (OR 1.67, p=0.002) and incurred $22,643 more in adjusted charges compared with White hospitalizations. Self-pay or uninsured status was associated with doubled mortality odds (OR 2.01, p<0.001). Enhanced clinical phenotyping underscores that Sjögren's syndrome is a complex, multisystem disease with a substantial inpatient burden. While SS-associated hospitalizations present with high baseline comorbidities, in-hospital mortality is strongly associated with acute complications, particularly respiratory failure, sepsis, stroke, and interstitial lung disease. Future clinical pathways should prioritize vigilant management of these vulnerabilities while addressing the structural and socioeconomic disparities associated with unequal outcomes.

items.title: Subcutaneous methotrexate for treating rheumatoid arthritis in Portugal: a cost-utility analysis versus current practice.
items.abstract: This study evaluated the cost-utility of subcutaneous versus oral methotrexate for rheumatoid arthritis (RA) management in Portugal. A cost-utility analysis (CUA) was conducted over a lifetime horizon from the Portuguese National Health Service perspective, adapting a model previously published for the United Kingdom. Patients were modelled to transition through lines of therapy including conventional synthetic, followed by biologic and targeted synthetic disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (DMARDs). In the base case, first-line subcutaneous methotrexate was compared with first-line oral methotrexate, while a scenario analysis explored second-line subcutaneous methotrexate use, after failing first-line oral methotrexate. Clinical, quality-of-life, and cost data were sourced from the literature, using Portuguese data where available. Projected costs and benefits were combined in net monetary benefit (NMB) estimates, evaluated against a willingness-to-pay threshold of €50,000 per quality-adjusted life-year (QALY) gained. The robustness of results was explored in sensitivity and scenario analyses. First-line subcutaneous methotrexate was projected to yield an additional 0.25 life-years and 0.55 QALYs, while reducing total costs by €11,108 over patients' lifetimes, relative to first-line oral methotrexate. Using subcutaneous methotrexate after first-line oral methotrexate was associated with gains in life expectancy (+0.54 life-years) and quality-adjusted life expectancy (+1.19 QALYs), while also reducing projected costs (-€25,892). In both analyses, subcutaneous methotrexate was therefore associated with improved effectiveness and reduced total costs. The corresponding NMBs were €38,821 and €85,485, respectively. Health gains resulted from more patient time spent on active treatment, with improved disease control, and consequently better health-related quality of life and reduced mortality risk. Improved disease control also implied reduced hospitalization costs, with costs further reduced due to delaying, or avoiding, costly biologics, which offset higher subcutaneous methotrexate acquisition costs. Sensitivity and scenario analyses confirmed base case results, including for different later-line biologic treatments, clinical response data, and time horizons. This CUA evaluated the value-for money of subcutaneous versus oral methotrexate for RA management in Portugal and found that subcutaneous methotrexate is likely a cost-effective strategy, with the potential to reduce healthcare expenditure and improve patient outcomes. These findings support consideration of wider adoption of subcutaneous methotrexate within Portuguese clinical practice.

items.title: Distinct clinical profiles of methotrexate intolerance and hepatotoxicity in psoriatic arthritis.
items.abstract: Methotrexate (MTX) is the most widely used conventional DMARD for psoriatic arthritis (PsA), but intolerance and hepatotoxicity often limit its long-term use. This study aimed to describe the prevalence and clinical correlates of MTX intolerance and hepatotoxicity in PsA patients. We conducted a retrospective study on adults with PsA who were exposed to MTX. Demographic, clinical, and treatment data were retrieved from electronic medical records. Intolerance was defined as discontinuation or dose reduction due to adverse effects, while hepatotoxicity was defined as discontinuation or dose reduction due to persistent liver enzyme elevation (≥2 times the upper limit of normal). Independent associations were explored using multivariable logistic regression. Among the 341 patients included, MTX intolerance occurred in 26.7% and hepatotoxicity in 10.3%. Bivariate analysis showed that intolerance was associated with female sex, shorter psoriasis-arthritis delay, enthesitis, higher use of csDMARDs and ts/bDMARDs, and lower persistence of TNF and IL-17 inhibitors. No independent predictors of intolerance were identified. Hepatotoxicity was linked to male sex, dactylitis, hypertension, hyperuricemia, and treatment-refractory PsA. In multivariable analysis, hepatotoxicity was independently associated with arterial hypertension (OR 4.40; p 0.007) and treatment-refractory PsA (OR 6.23; p 0.016), and inversely associated with intolerance (OR 0.09; p 0.023). MTX intolerance and hepatotoxicity in PsA were associated with distinct clinical patterns: intolerance predominates in women and is associated with frequent therapeutic modifications, whereas hepatotoxicity is more common in men with metabolic comorbidities and treatment-refractory disease. Recognizing these patterns may help optimize MTX safety, guide therapeutic decisions, and enhance treatment persistence.

items.title: LLM-supported self-diagnosis and self-treatment of familial Mediterranean fever: a case report.
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being used by patients to seek explanations for persistent or unexplained symptoms. However, their impact on real-world diagnostic pathways and patient behavior remains poorly understood. We report the case of a 34-year-old male of Egyptian origin with recurrent episodes of fever, severe migratory abdominal pain, arthralgia, myalgia, and intermittent erythematous skin lesions since early childhood. Despite almost 3 decades of extensive investigations, no unifying diagnosis had been established. During an iterative dialogue with the LLM DeepSeek in June 2025, the differential diagnosis was progressively refined toward familial Mediterranean fever (FMF). Although the model repeatedly recommended specialist assessment, it also provided specific information regarding genetic testing and colchicine treatment. The patient subsequently arranged genetic testing independently and obtained colchicine in Egypt, initiating treatment without prior specialist assessment at 0.5 mg twice daily. His inflammatory attacks ceased completely. However, liver enzymes increased, prompting temporary treatment discontinuation and dose reduction. FMF was thereafter confirmed by specialist assessment based on the characteristic clinical phenotype, family history, genotype, and response to colchicine. This case illustrates how patient-facing LLMs may facilitate recognition of rare autoinflammatory diseases. However, confident diagnostic language combined with actionable treatment advice may also encourage unsupervised testing and self-medication, underscoring the need for clear safety boundaries and specialist confirmation.

items.title: Tregs transduced with a Ro60-reactive TCR have increased immunosuppressive functions in Sjögren's disease.
items.abstract: Sjögren's disease (SjD) is a T cell-driven autoimmune condition strongly associated with the HLA-DRB1∗03:01 allele and autoantibodies against the Ro60 protein. Previous studies have identified deficiencies in regulatory T cells (Treg) in patients, indicating a breakdown in immune tolerance. Current treatments remain limited to symptomatic relief or broad immunosuppression, without addressing the underlying immune dysregulation. In this study, we present the first preclinical evidence supporting a TCR-engineered Treg (TCR-Treg) therapy specifically targeting SjD. We designed a TCR-Treg that recognizes a dominant epitope of the Ro60 antigen (Ro60 369-383 ) presented by HLA-DRB1∗03:01 and demonstrate that these cells can selectively suppress autoreactive T cells more effectively than polyclonal Treg. These findings underscore the pathogenic significance of the Ro-HLA-DRB1∗03:01 axis and provide proof-of-concept for a targeted, antigen-specific Treg therapy. This approach offers a promising strategy to restore immune tolerance and represents a potential disease-modifying treatment for genetically defined subsets of patients with SjD.

items.title: Functional characterization of genetic variants associated with response to tumor necrosis factor inhibitors in psoriatic arthritis patients.
items.abstract: Psoriatic arthritis is a chronic, progressive inflammatory disease associated with psoriasis, affecting joints, entheses, and the axial skeleton. Treatment options have evolved from broad immunosuppressive therapies to targeted biologic agents. These therapies are generally safe and effective, but patient response varies considerably, emphasizing the importance of pharmacogenetic studies in the identification of variants that predict treatment response. This review explores the potential functional significance and causality of variants that were associated with response to tumor necrosis factor inhibitors by assessing their regulatory impact on gene expression, alternative splicing, transcription factor binding, chromatin state, and chromatin accessibility, using a combination of in silico resources. This integrated analysis revealed novel regulatory roles for specific variants. The variants rs1801274 in FCGR2A and rs396991 in FCGR3A have established biological roles in inflammation. The risk allele of variant rs767455 in TNFRSF1A correlates with increased TNFRSF1A expression and favors the splicing event that generates a TNFRSF1A soluble isoform lacking exon 6, resulting in increased inflammation. The variant rs20575 within TNFRSF10A correlates with the expression of the nearby inflammatory TNFRSF10D gene. The TNF variant rs1800610 correlates with changes in the expression of many nearby genes of the Human Leukocyte Antigen region. The variant rs610604, located within TNFAIP3, correlates with changes in the expression and splicing isoforms of WAKMAR2, a lncRNA with an anti-inflammatory role. In conclusion, the majority of variants associated with treatment response show strong evidence of a potential role in inflammation and psoriatic arthritis and may serve as clinical biomarkers pending replication and functional validation.

items.title: Elderly-onset rheumatoid arthritis versus polymyalgia rheumatica: A systematic review and meta-analysis on pathophysiology, diagnosis and clinical progression.
items.abstract: Elderly-onset rheumatoid arthritis (EORA) and polymyalgia rheumatica (PMR) are among the most frequent inflammatory rheumatic diseases in patients over 50, yet their clinical differentiation, particularly when EORA presents with polymyalgic onset, poses a common diagnostic challenge. This systematic review aimed to identify the pathophysiological, clinical, imaging and treatment-response features that distinguish EORA from PMR. MEDLINE, CENTRAL and Scopus (inception to January 2026), with supplementary searches of LILACS, Google Scholar and trial registries (June 2026) were searched, including studies that compared EORA with PMR or reported separately extractable data for both; risk of bias was appraised with design-specific tools and the evidence weighted accordingly. Seventy-one studies across four domains were included: pathophysiology (22 studies), clinical presentation and final diagnosis at follow-up (24 studies), imaging (21 studies), and treatment response (4 studies). Genetically, in one low risk of bias study that stratified EORA by rheumatoid factor status, PMR and seronegative EORA shared HLA-DRB1*13/*14 associations, a pattern distinct from the shared epitope-driven susceptibility of seropositive RA. However, divergent metabolomic signatures suggest different downstream inflammatory mechanisms. An exploratory random-effects meta-analysis yielded a pooled PMR-to-RA reclassification rate of 7% (95% CI 4-12%; 9 studies), narrowing to 4% (95% CI 2-7%) in methodologically robust studies, though rates of reclassification to RA were considerably higher (up to 20%) when patients with undifferentiated polymyalgic presentations were included. Peripheral arthritis occurred in 28% of PMR patients (95% CI 20-35%; 6 studies), with a significant difference between baseline prevalence (21%) and cumulative incidence over follow-up (34%) on subgroup meta-analysis (p = 0.026), and was characteristically transient and glucocorticoid-responsive, whereas persistent synovitis involving wrists and small joints was associated with reclassification to RA. On imaging, evidence from low-to-moderate risk of bias, ultrasound studies showed that shoulder findings overlapped substantially between conditions, whereas bilateral hip synovitis was significantly more frequent in PMR (47% vs 0% in RA), suggesting the hip as a stronger proximal informative site. However, distal joint synovitis demonstrated the highest discriminatory value, with the presence of at least one among RF positivity, hand grey-scale ≥2, or hand power Doppler ≥1 achieving 89% sensitivity and 93% specificity for EORA identification. This review highlights that the distinction between EORA and PMR cannot be reliably established at a single time point and that longitudinal reassessment integrating clinical, serological, and imaging findings remains essential for the differential diagnosis. However, the evidence is limited by clinical and methodological heterogeneity and the predominance of observational designs.

items.title: Risk of demyelinating events associated with TNF-inhibitors compared with conventional synthetic disease modifying anti-rheumatic drugs in rheumatoid arthritis: results from the French National Health Data System.
items.abstract: To assess the risk of demyelinating events of TNF-inhibitors compared to conventional synthetic disease modifying anti-rheumatic drugs, in rheumatoid arthritis in real life setting. In this nationwide population-based cohort study conducted in the French National Health Data System, adult patients with rheumatoid arthritis, with no history of demyelinating event, naïve to conventional treatments and TNF-inhibitors, were included at conventional treatment initiation between 2008 and 2022 and followed until December 31, 2023. The primary endpoint was the occurrence of an incident coded demyelinating event (central or peripheral), identified by International Classification of Diseases (10 th revision) codes. The association with TNF-inhibitors was assessed using a marginal structural Cox model weighted by inverse probability of treatment weights, with time-dependent exposure. Overall, 214,892 patients with rheumatoid arthritis (70.6% women, median age 58.8 years) incident users of conventional treatments were included, with a median follow-up time of 7.4 years; among them, 40,139 patients initiated a TNF-inhibitor during follow-up. A total of 562 coded demyelinating events occurred under treatments exposure between 2008 and 2023. The weighted cumulative incidence of demyelinating events at 10 years was 0.32% (95%CI 0.29-0.36) with conventional treatments, and 0.50% (95%CI 0.36-0.63) with TNF-inhibitors. Exposure to TNF-inhibitors was statistically significantly associated with an increased risk of coded demyelinating events compared with conventional treatments, hazard ratio (HR) 1.47 (95% CI, 1.11-1.95). Demyelinating events are rare in patients with rheumatoid arthritis. This study found a statistically significant increased risk of coded demyelinating event associated with TNF-inhibitors exposure compared with conventional treatments.

items.title: Can serial ANCA testing be used to predict the risk of relapse in patients with granulomatosis with polyangiitis? A single-center cohort study.
items.abstract: To investigate whether serial ANCA testing could predict the risk of relapse in patients with granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA). We conducted an observational cohort study of patients with GPA, who were followed in a referral vasculitis center. For enrolment, patients had to have ANCA-positive GPA, at least one measurement of ANCA titer by ELISA in the 12 months preceding disease inactivity, with a subsequent disease activity evaluation in the following 18 months. The primary endpoint was time to relapse within the 18 months of follow-up. We compared patients with and without increases in ANCA titer and adjusted for potential confounders by direct standardisation based on Cox regression. In 125 GPA patients (PR3-ANCA: 105; MPO-ANCA: 20), the adjusted relapse rate was 31.0% (95% confidence interval [CI] 11.2-54.4%) in 23 patient-periods for the Increase group versus 25.6% (95% CI 19.7-31.9%) in 355 patient-periods for the No increase group. In PR3-ANCA patients, the corresponding relapse rates were 32.1% (95% CI 11.9-54.1%) versus 26.4% (95% CI 20.4-34.0%). Following a doubling of ANCA titer, the relapse rates were 36.2% (95% CI 15.1-61.4%) versus 25.3% (95% CI 19.6-31.6%). The adjusted risk of major relapse was 24.9% (95% CI 7.0-45.5%) in the Increase group versus 16.5% (95% CI 12.3-21.9%) in the No increase group. In GPA patients, an increase in ANCA, a doubling of ANCA or an increase in PR3-ANCA alone was unable to predict relapse at 18 months sufficiently reliably to consider treatment escalation on an individual basis.

items.title: Traditional Chinese Medicine as Adjunctive Care in Cancer and Rheumatoid Arthritis: A Narrative Review of Shared Frameworks and Evidence Gaps.
items.abstract: Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) has increasingly been investigated as an adjunctive approach to conventional treatment in chronic and complex diseases, including cancer and rheumatoid arthritis (RA). Although cancer and RA differ substantially in pathogenesis and therapeutic goals, both are associated with persistent symptom burden, treatment-related adverse effects, impaired physical function, psychological distress, and long-term supportive-care needs. This narrative review evaluates TCM within this shared adjunctive-care framework while maintaining disease-specific interpretation of the available evidence. In cancer, TCM-related interventions have been investigated for supportive symptom management, pain relief, treatment tolerance, quality-of-life improvement, and potential modulation of biological processes, including apoptosis, angiogenesis, immune regulation, invasion, metastasis, and multidrug resistance. In RA, Chinese herbal medicines, acupuncture, and related approaches have been evaluated for their potential effects on pain, inflammation, physical function, bone remodeling, and early disease-related processes. TCM-related mind-body practices, such as qigong and tai chi, may also provide psychological support, whereas mindfulness-based interventions are considered supportive-care strategies rather than TCM interventions. Current evidence ranges from mechanistic and preclinical studies to observational studies, single-arm clinical studies, randomized controlled trials, systematic reviews, and meta-analyses, with substantial variation in methodological quality. Overall, TCM should be considered a potential complement to, rather than a replacement for, established oncological or rheumatological treatment. Further well-designed clinical studies, standardized interventions, rigorous quality control, safety monitoring, and clinically meaningful outcome assessment are required to define its appropriate role in multidisciplinary care.

items.title: Understanding the Evidence Gaps in the Epidemiology and Burden of Lupus Nephritis and Membranous Nephropathy: A Targeted Literature Review.
items.abstract: Lupus nephritis (LN) and membranous nephropathy (MN) are associated with progression to chronic kidney disease and end-stage renal disease (ESRD), but evidence describing the full disease burden across countries remains limited and fragmented. This targeted literature review (TLR) aimed to characterize the disease burden of LN and MN, including epidemiology and clinical, humanistic, and economic outcomes, and identify unmet needs and current knowledge gaps. A targeted, nonsystematic search of MEDLINE and EMBASE was conducted for English-language articles published between January 2013 and August 2023 in the United States (US), the United Kingdom, Germany, France, China, and Japan. Searches identified 26 relevant articles for LN and 11 for MN. LN epidemiology studies were limited to the US; incidence was estimated at 1:100 000, with higher risk in older individuals, females, and African Americans. MN is rare, with reported annual incidences of 10 to 12 per million in North America and 2 to 17 per million in Europe. Prevalence appears to be increasing for both diseases. LN was associated with substantial progression to ESRD, with 21.1% to 36.8% of patients progressing within 5 to 10 years. ESRD represented a major economic driver, with US monthly costs of approximately $15 000 per patient with LN. MN burden data were more limited but indicated risk of severe long-term renal complications and ESRD. Humanistic burden data were sparse; reported health-related quality-of-life impacts include renal symptom domains not captured by generic instruments, indicating a need for disease-specific measures. Despite evidence of substantial burden, important gaps remain. Epidemiological data were geographically limited, with incidence varying widely, potentially reflecting differences in populations, treatment eras, and ethnicity. Long-term data beyond 5 to 10 years were limited, and robust syntheses evaluating prognostic factors influencing progression to ESRD were lacking. The absence of renal-specific patient-reported outcome measures and inconsistent clinical definitions further limits comparability and treatment value assessment. LN and MN are associated with significant clinical, economic, and humanistic burden, especially for patients with ESRD, but certainty and generalizability are limited by the focused TLR methods and heterogeneous evidence base. More robust data would help characterize long-term outcomes and support more informed value assessments.

items.title: Anaphylaxis Following Intravenous Methylprednisolone Sodium Succinate: A Case Report.
items.abstract: Immediate hypersensitivity to systemic corticosteroids is rare but potentially life-threatening, and it may be overlooked when the cardiovascular presentation is atypical. Identifying the responsible determinant, whether the corticosteroid molecule, a solubilizing ester, or a formulation excipient, is often difficult. A 45-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis developed a generalized pruritic, erythematous, raised eruption, dyspnea, hypoxemia, bradycardia, and reduced consciousness within 5 minutes of starting intravenous methylprednisolone sodium succinate 250 mg. The infusion was stopped, and symptoms resolved after intramuscular epinephrine 0.4 mg. Approximately 7 hours later, because the reaction was considered unlikely to be allergic, the same formulation was re-administered in two graded steps (25%, then 75%) under continuous monitoring and direct physician supervision. This high-risk re-exposure after clinically convincing anaphylaxis reproduced the cutaneous and respiratory features, again with bradycardia (heart rate 51 beats/min) and hypoxemia (oxygen saturation 88%), and required intramuscular epinephrine 0.3 mg, an intravenous antihistamine, oxygen, and a bronchodilator. Serum tryptase and formal allergy testing were not obtained. She later reported tolerating oral prednisolone, with no recurrent symptoms during 3 months of follow-up. Recurrence on re-exposure supports anaphylaxis to the administered methylprednisolone formulation, but without confirmatory testing the reaction cannot be attributed to methylprednisolone itself, the succinate ester, or an excipient. This patient-safety case shows that bradycardia does not exclude anaphylaxis; that a graded challenge is a diagnostic test, not desensitization, and is not a recommended strategy after convincing anaphylaxis; and that the exact implicated formulation should be documented instead of a nonspecific steroid-allergy label.

items.title: Antineutrophil Cytoplasmic Antibodies: Integrating History, Pathogenesis, and Modern Diagnostics.
items.abstract: Antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (ANCA) define a distinct group of small-vessel vasculitides collectively termed ANCA-associated vasculitis (AAV). Since their initial recognition as immunofluorescence patterns, ANCA have evolved into well-characterized pathogenic autoantibodies directed primarily against proteinase 3 (PR3) and myeloperoxidase (MPO). This review integrates the historical evolution of ANCA discovery with current understanding of disease pathogenesis and contemporary diagnostic practice. We summarize key biological mechanisms underlying AAV, including genetic susceptibility, epigenetic dysregulation, neutrophil priming, complement activation via the alternative pathway, and neutrophil extracellular trap formation, which together drive endothelial injury and necrotizing vasculitis. Recognition of PR3 ANCA and MPO ANCA as pathogenic entities has reshaped disease classification and supports the concept of biologically distinct disease subsets. In parallel, laboratory diagnostics have undergone a major paradigm shift. We critically review the transition from indirect immunofluorescence-first algorithms to immunoassay-first strategies endorsed by the 2017 revised international consensus, highlighting the improved diagnostic performance of contemporary antigen-specific immunoassays. The roles of automated immunofluorescence, biochip mosaic platforms, and multiparametric testing are discussed within harmonized diagnostic workflows. Emphasis is placed on strict clinical gating, quantitative antibody interpretation, and likelihood ratio-based reporting to enhance diagnostic accuracy and reduce false-positive results. By integrating historical, biological, and diagnostic perspectives, this review provides a practical reference framework for evidence-based ANCA testing and interpretation in clinical practice.

items.title: Peripheral ossifying fibroma mimicking oral Kaposi's sarcoma in an immunosuppressed patient with Behçet's disease: a case report.
items.abstract: Kaposi's sarcoma (KS) is an HHV-8-associated angioproliferative neoplasm occurring preferentially in immunosuppressed individuals, with oral involvement documented in up to 65% of HIV/AIDS patients. Several benign reactive gingival lesions, including peripheral ossifying fibroma (POF), may clinically mimic oral KS, creating a significant diagnostic challenge. In patients with established systemic KS, newly detected oral lesions carry a high risk of diagnostic anchoring bias, making HHV-8 (LANA-1) immunohistochemistry indispensable for definitive diagnosis. A 57-year-old male with Behçet's disease under long-term corticosteroid therapy (15 mg/day) and histologically confirmed cutaneous KS was referred for a painless gingival nodule evolving over 6 years. Intraoral examination revealed a well-demarcated, firm, pink, non-bleeding nodular lesion on the lingual mandibular gingiva, without bone involvement on panoramic radiography. The atypical clinical presentation prompted complete surgical excision under local anesthesia. Histopathology demonstrated a benign fibrocellular proliferation with focal mineralized deposits consistent with POF. HHV-8 LANA-1 immunohistochemistry, performed on the Autostainer Link 48 DAKO platform using the EnVision K5007 system, showed absent HHV-8 expression, definitively excluding oral KS. Healing was uneventful with no recurrence at 6 months. The coexistence of systemic KS and iatrogenic immunosuppression introduced a powerful cognitive prior - diagnostic anchoring bias - directing clinical reasoning toward mucosal KS despite four atypical features: pink coloration, firm consistency, absence of spontaneous bleeding, and 6-year indolent evolution. Negative HHV-8 immunostaining was decisive, confirming that oral lesions in KS patients are not necessarily mucosal disease. This case reinforces the principle that histopathological and immunohistochemical analysis must systematically override clinical gestalt in this setting. Early biopsy combined with HHV-8 (LANA-1) immunohistochemistry is essential when evaluating oral nodular lesions in immunosuppressed patients with established KS, to prevent diagnostic anchoring bias and avoid unnecessary oncologic investigations.
